implementation_engines.name: Linear SVM/tf-idf/SPECTER
implementation_engines.role: personal preference scoring, not inferred graph store

backend.source_model_description: Semantic Scholar literature KG and existing research feeds; ensemble linear SVM models using tf-idf title/abstract features and SPECTER embeddings; batching of base-entity scores and model retraining after preference changes

tasks: Two literature tasks, five papers and five authors; logs/interviews each n10, subsets not new cohorts

descriptions.interaction: Curate research feeds; use a feed as a lens; browse papers and authors; hover to inspect relevance summaries/explanations; follow recommended authors and sort paper lists by relevance
descriptions.guidance: Personalized relevance scores, author recommendations and ranking; count-over-threshold summaries; LIMEADE keyword explanations; randomized recommendations among authors with fewer relevant papers
descriptions.visualisation: Embedded author bar-chart overviews, paper relevance squares/scores, author recommendation dots and hover explanations in the existing Semantic Scholar interface
descriptions.backend: Semantic Scholar literature KG and existing research feeds; ensemble linear SVM models using tf-idf title/abstract features and SPECTER embeddings; batching of base-entity scores and model retraining after preference changes
descriptions.evaluation: Counterbalanced within-subjects remote comparison with a production baseline; separate offline approximation experiment

report_level_evaluation.design: Counterbalanced within-subjects remote comparison with a production baseline; separate offline approximation experiment
report_level_evaluation.participants: user study n: 15; interaction logs n: 10; interview n: 10; background: Graduate students in computing-related fields;4 active Semantic Scholar users and11 trained to curate feeds at least one week before the study; formative pilots: n: 17; population: Semantic Scholar designers/researchers; n: 13; population: Current Semantic Scholar users; offline data: 346 real feeds,30 authors per feed,20% test split
report_level_evaluation.tasks: Two short literature-review tasks using different research feeds: select5 new papers and5 new authors in each condition; inspect multiple lenses afterwards
report_level_evaluation.comparators: Semantic Scholar without FeedLens features; offline summary embeddings compared with exhaustive per-paper scoring and mean-count baseline
report_level_evaluation.measures: NASA-TLX, SUS, system logs, task duration, relevance/diversity/novelty/obviousness of selected items, subjective item ratings, feature usefulness and thematic interviews; offline RMSE/count approximation and speedup
report_level_evaluation.results: FeedLens SUS84(SD8.6) vs77.3(SD12.5), p<.01; cognitive-load ratings2.4(SD1) vs3.3(SD1.3) on1–5 scale. Logged system-wide interactions365.4 vs96.5 on average; author-centric interactions123 vs5.5, p<<.001. Selected authors had13 vs6 relevant papers on average. Task duration15.8 vs10.76min; increased time was interpreted as engagement. Other final-list diversity/novelty and subjective metrics differed only marginally.8/10 interviewees preferred FeedLens. Offline K=sqrt(n) summary embeddings:12x speedup,RMSE4.33,88.50% counts within approximately factor2.; limits: Only one domain and one additional entity type were implemented/evaluated; small technical sample; five participants lacked logs; feed curation and different feed topics affect comparisons; shortened tasks; within-subjects carryover possible. Relevance includes the recommender’s own score, so it is not independent ground truth. Supplementary metric tables were not available in this local file; summary embeddings were future deployment work rather than the evaluated UI backend.; The reported20x author-centric engagement includes hover interactions; comparable author-homepage views increased about3x.; Extra time spent exploring is not evidence of faster task completion.; The formulation supports arbitrary entity types, but the evaluated prototype adds authors to paper exploration.
report_level_evaluation.limitations: Only one domain and one additional entity type were implemented/evaluated; small technical sample; five participants lacked logs; feed curation and different feed topics affect comparisons; shortened tasks; within-subjects carryover possible. Relevance includes the recommender’s own score, so it is not independent ground truth. Supplementary metric tables were not available in this local file; summary embeddings were future deployment work rather than the evaluated UI backend.; The reported20x author-centric engagement includes hover interactions; comparable author-homepage views increased about3x.; Extra time spent exploring is not evidence of faster task completion.; The formulation supports arbitrary entity types, but the evaluated prototype adds authors to paper exploration.
